title: Remediation iteration record
description: iterations/<n>.json. One iteration of the fix-and-recheck loop: which findings it took, what it changed, and what the re-review said afterwards. The re-review is the check on the fix, so an iteration that claims progress without a recheck verdict is rejected rather than believed.

iteration.description: One-based position in the bound, so a record read on its own says where in the budget it happened.

findings_sha256.description: Digest of the findings this iteration triaged. A later iteration reading a different set is working from a review this record does not describe.

triaged.description: Every finding this iteration considered, with what it decided. Coverage against the review's own findings is checked imperatively, since the schema cannot see the other file.

triage.description: One finding's disposition for this iteration. Dismissing needs a reason; fixing needs the change named, because the next re-review is what tests the claim.

action.description: `deferred` postpones within the loop and leaves the finding for a later iteration; `dismissed` ends it, which is why only the lowest severity may use it.

allOf.description: Only a minor finding may be dismissed. A blocking or major finding carries a fix obligation, so dismissing one is how a loop terminates with the defect intact.

recheck.description: The re-review that tested this iteration's fixes. Its counts come from the new review run, not from the fixer's own judgement of its work.

ran.description: The exact command that produced the counts, so the verdict can be reproduced rather than taken on trust.
